correctness.rationale: The proof uses an explicit diagonal sign unitary from a bipartition. It fixes the band-diagonal kinetic and intra-band parts and negates every nonzero off-diagonal interaction block, giving exact unitary equivalence. Positivity and the full spectrum are unitary invariants, and the critical-temperature definition therefore gives exact evenness. The converse gauge criterion is equivalent to requiring a phase difference of pi on every graph edge, possible exactly when every cycle is even.

value.rationale: The source makes the attractive-versus-repulsive sign question central and notes that sign dependence can emerge with three or more bands. The result replaces band count by a natural structural invariant: every bipartite coupling network, including arbitrarily large trees and even-cycle networks, is exactly sign-blind at the entire linearized spectral level. It also identifies odd cycles as the exact obstruction to this gauge mechanism.
